index.title: Learn ZudoJS — from JavaScript to production backends
index.description: A free, hands-on path from your first line of JavaScript to Node.js, backend fundamentals, TypeScript and production ZudoJS applications. Every example runs in your browser or on your computer, with the real output shown.
index.heading: Learn ZudoJS
index.lead: Start with plain JavaScript, learn Node.js and how backends work, move to TypeScript, then build real backends with ZudoJS and take them to production. ZudoJS is the destination, not the starting point: every lesson shows the real output of the code, in the terminal on the page or on your own computer.

advanced.label: Advanced
advanced.summary: Learn it when your application needs it.

production.label: Production
production.summary: Learn it when you prepare a real application for deployment.

parts.title: Start here
parts.summary: What this course is, the tools a developer uses every day, how a program runs, how the web works, and your first program.

parts.title: JavaScript fundamentals
parts.summary: The language itself: values, operators, decisions, loops, functions, arrays, objects, classes, errors, asynchronous code and modules.

parts.title: Node.js and npm
parts.summary: JavaScript on the server: the runtime and event loop, files and streams, npm packages, and an HTTP server with no framework at all.

parts.title: Backend fundamentals
parts.summary: HTTP in depth, REST API design, databases and SQL with PostgreSQL, Git and GitHub, and testing.

parts.title: TypeScript
parts.summary: Add types to the same JavaScript: basic types, functions, interfaces and unions, generics, advanced and utility types, classes, modules, and where types stop and runtime checks begin.

parts.title: Project: a TypeScript backend
parts.summary: Build a BookStore API with TypeScript and no framework, and feel the problems a framework exists to solve.

parts.title: Architecture and frameworks
parts.summary: Controllers, services, repositories and dependency direction, then what a framework actually does for you.

parts.title: Meet ZudoJS
parts.summary: What ZudoJS is, your first ZudoJS code, and the Task API project you build for the rest of the course.

parts.title: The ZudoJS core
parts.summary: The runtime and lifecycle, dependency injection, HTTP routing and middleware, configuration, validation and errors.

parts.title: Data
parts.summary: Databases, repositories and migrations, storage abstractions, and transactions.

parts.title: Users and security
parts.summary: Passwords, JWTs and sessions, OAuth sign-in, permissions, and the security layer every public API needs.

parts.title: Events, messages and background work
parts.summary: Caching, events, messaging, CQRS, queues, scheduled jobs and serialization.

parts.title: APIs and services
parts.summary: Calling other services with RPC, one operation served over many transports, and OpenAPI documents generated from your code.

parts.title: Testing and observability
parts.summary: Test a ZudoJS application end to end, log in a structured way, and see inside a running system with metrics and traces.

parts.title: Architecture with ZudoJS
parts.summary: From one application to a modular monolith, then to microservices, with the communication tools ZudoJS already has.

parts.title: Production
parts.summary: Production engineering, deployment with Docker, the ShopFlow capstone, and the final challenge.
